transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Atlas CTO), Elena Ruiz (ML Eng), Priya Kapoor (Head of Security), Ravi Patel (PM)

Summary: quick migration walkthrough 	6 parity mapping from OpenAI -> Redwood, show API examples, console, Optimize recommendations, and security notes.

[00:00] Samantha Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, um i'm sam from redwood, i'm the AE on this account, we also have diego who will run through the technical demo. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Mark Chen: good, thanks, excited to see this; we've been evaluating options to move off OpenAI for cost reasons and some compliance stuff.
[00:14] Diego Ramirez: awesome. quick agenda: parity mapping for chat/generation, embeddings migration, function/tool-calling equivalents, streaming behavior, console + optimize features, then q&a and next steps.
[00:30] Elena Ruiz: quick note 	6 our primary use case is chat assistants in prod (healthcare triage), lots of short chats and embedding search for docs. latency is important.
[00:38] Samantha Lee: great 	6 that'll guide the demo.
[02:05] Diego Ramirez: okay starting with API parity. OpenAI's chat completions map to Redwood's /v1/chat endpoint. the request shape is very similar 	6 messages, roles, temperature; we also add model variants in the model param. example here: (shared link: https://redwood.example.com/parity/spreadsheet)
[02:25] Diego Ramirez: note, Redwood supports function/tool calling like OpenAI. small difference: we expose a more explicit schema validation path in the SDK and console to validate structured outputs.
[03:10] Elena Ruiz: are there differences in streaming tokens behavior? we rely on streaming to reduce perceived latency.
[03:18] Diego Ramirez: good question; streaming is available and we preserve chunked token events. tiny caveat 	6 depending on quantization profile, you might see slightly different tokenization boundaries, but from an app perspective it's compatible.
[04:01] Mark Chen: what's the model catalog look like, do we host open weights or do you provide hosted models?
[04:09] Samantha Lee: we provide curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. for enterprise you can choose hosted API or Dedicated pools or Private (VPC/on-prem). Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and consistent latency.
[04:45] Diego Ramirez: demoing quick parity snippet: (reads code) you replace openai.ChatCompletion.create with redwood.chat.create, same messages array, and the SDK maps automatically. here's an example of embeddings 	6 OpenAI embedding -> redwood.embeddings.create. there are small parameter name differences, e.g., "input" still present but we support batch inputs and auto-batching at the runtime.
[05:30] Priya Kapoor: security 	6 how do you handle data at rest and KMS? we're subject to HIPAA-ish controls and need customer-managed keys.
[05:39] Samantha Lee: we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. Hosted can use our managed KMS but for enterprise Private you bring your KMS and we integrate 	6 we also have audit logs and retention controls. we'll share the SOC 2 + security whitepaper after the call.
[06:15] Diego Ramirez: one thing to watch when migrating: prompt-token counting and pricing differences 	6 Redwood Optimize provides batch suggestions and KV prefix caching to reduce per-token cost.
[07:02] Ravi Patel: can you explain KV cache 	6 our current system stores past context to speed up completions.
[07:10] Diego Ramirez: yes, KV cache is our term for key/value cache for attention keys; sometimes transcripts say K V cash 	6 but it's cache. Redwood can persist prefix KV caches for repeated prompts which reduces token compute; this is configurable per-route.
[08:00] Mark Chen: about latency 	6 if we move from OpenAI to Redwood Hosted, what SLOs are typical?
[08:08] Diego Ramirez: for hosted API we publish median latency numbers per model; Dedicated gives SLA-backed latency guarantees (configurable). for your workload we'd recommend Dedicated reserved pool to achieve <150ms median for short chats, but we'll benchmark.
[09:22] Samantha Lee: sharing screen 	6 quick tour of Console: per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and rollout controls for canary/A-B. you can pin model versions, set fallback policy if a model is down.
[10:05] Elena Ruiz: is there an automated parity tool to translate prompts or system messages?
[10:13] Diego Ramirez: not automated translation of prompts but we provide examples and a parity spreadsheet that maps OpenAI params to Redwood params and calls out behavior differences (we just shared link in chat).
[11:40] Mark Chen: embeddings migration 	6 we currently use OpenAI text-embedding-3-small. how does Redwood handle vector dims and similarity?
[11:48] Diego Ramirez: we support the common dims; if you bring embeddings from OpenAI, we can host the same model or recommend equivalent open models. similarity computation is up to your vector DB; Redwood's embeddings follow same L2/cosine norms. Optimize can recommend quantized embedding models to save cost.
[13:05] Priya Kapoor: compliance again 	6 can we get an on-prem option?
[13:12] Samantha Lee: yes, Private can be VPC-connected or full on-prem with air-gapped package for the most regulated customers. we have a professional services path to deploy.
[14:40] Ravi Patel: about billing 	6 is pricing per token similar to market? we need predictable monthly costs.
[14:50] Samantha Lee: hosted is usage-based per token; Dedicated offers reserved capacity contracts for predictable monthly billing. we'll include example pricing tiers in the spreadsheet.
[16:05] Diego Ramirez: demoing a live API call (note: occasional transcription artifacts possible):
[16:12] [screen] curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
[16:20] Diego Ramirez: you can stream the response with chunked transfers; in SDKs the stream API is almost identical to OpenAI's.
[18:00] Elena Ruiz: okay on function calling, does Redwood support nested JSON outputs and validation? we've had issues with inconsistent JSON from models.
[18:10] Diego Ramirez: yes, we have schema validation hooks; the runtime can coerce or reject responses that don't match, and the console shows mismatches as a structured error. that helps in regression testing.
[19:30] Mark Chen: we've also used Anthropic in a few experiments. anything special when migrating from Anthropic->Redwood?
[19:38] Samantha Lee: similar story 	6 message format mapping is supported, but Anthropic's safety/assistant role semantics can differ; our parity doc lists known differences.
[21:00] Diego Ramirez: now quick show of Optimize 	6 it suggests batching sizes, quantization profiles per model, and caching settings based on your observed pattern. you can run a simulated cost report to see potential savings.
[22:40] Ravi Patel: does Optimize recommend model quantization aggressiveness? any quality regressions we should expect?
[22:48] Diego Ramirez: yes, recommendations include quantization level and suggested eval prompts to validate quality. we also provide rollback and A-B via console to compare outputs before full rollout.
[24:05] Samantha Lee: shared artifact: parity spreadsheet (link), security whitepaper (link), and deployment checklist in the chat.
[25:10] Priya Kapoor: can we get more detail on data retention and deletion APIs? we need deletes to be auditable.
[25:18] Samantha Lee: yes 	6 we have deletion endpoints and audit logs; for Dedicated/Private we can shorten retention windows and provide on-demand purges. we'll include compliance appendix.
[26:50] Diego Ramirez: some migration gotchas to call out: tokenization differences can change counts slightly, streaming chunk boundaries differ, and function-calling field names may need small edits. but overall it's a 1:1 mapping for most workloads.
[28:00] Mark Chen: pilot timeline 	6 we want to do a 2-week pilot on Dedicated if results look good 	6 run benchmarks and cost estimates.
[28:08] Samantha Lee: great 	6 proposed next steps: 1) sam sends parity + pricing sheet, 2) diego runs perf benchmark with your sample, 3) security docs to priya, 4) schedule kickoff for pilot.
[30:15] Diego Ramirez: i'll note technical details for the benchmark: we need a representative traffic trace, sample prompt set, and a 1-2GB doc corpus for embeddings test. can you share that?
[30:27] Elena Ruiz: yes we'll prepare 	6 could you confirm the formats? currently we have ndjson for prompts and csv for embeddings.
[30:35] Diego Ramirez: ndjson for prompts is perfect; embeddings CSV is fine, we ingest. we'll send an S3 presigned link template.
[32:00] Ravi Patel: any concerns about vendor lock-in? we want to keep the ability to switch or run on prem later.
[32:10] Samantha Lee: that's a fair question 	6 Redwood's APIs are intentionally similar to major providers to lower lock-in friction; plus Private/on-prem allows you to run same runtime yourself.
[33:45] Priya Kapoor: audit logs detail 	6 do logs include token-level request data or just metadata?
[33:53] Samantha Lee: by default logs include request metadata; we can provide per-customer options for full request logs stored in your account for Dedicated/Private with KMS. we'll include the logging spec.
[35:00] Diego Ramirez: quick technical note 	6 model variants and kernel selection are handled by the runtime; you can pin a variant if you want stable perf and quality, or allow auto-selection for cost.
[36:20] Mark Chen: if we do Dedicated, what's the onboarding time?
[36:28] Samantha Lee: usually 2-4 weeks depending on provisioning and security review; Private on-prem is longer with professional services.
[37:10] Diego Ramirez: i'll follow up with a benchmark plan doc template.
[38:00] Mark Chen: ok let's talk about success criteria 	6 we need equal or better latency, <15% cost delta relative to OpenAI after Optimize, and no compliance gaps.
[38:12] Samantha Lee: noted 	6 we'll build the benchmark to measure those exact metrics.
[40:05] Ravi Patel: any references of customers in healthcare?
[40:12] Samantha Lee: yes we have a couple 	6 we'll share anonymized case studies.
[41:00] Priya Kapoor: last question 	6 SSO/SAML for console?
[41:07] Samantha Lee: yes, SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning in Enterprise.
[42:20] Samantha Lee: recap of next steps and owners, and we'll follow up with calendar invites. thanks everyone for the time.
[42:35] Mark Chen: thanks, appreciated.
[42:40] Elena Ruiz: thanks.
[42:45] Meeting end.

Artifacts shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/parity/spreadsheet, https://redwood.example.com/security/whitepaper.pdf, benchmark_plan_template.xlsx

Notes on transcription quality: medium 	6 minor mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V cash' in one section) and occasional speaker attribution issues.
